shots.alt: The Windows SmartScreen dialog 'Windows protected your PC' with More info expanded and the Run anyway button visible.
shots.notes: Run the installer on Windows 11: in the blue SmartScreen dialog click More info so the Run anyway button shows. Capture the dialog (Win+Shift+S, window snip). Needs the real Windows UI.

shots.alt: The Windows protected your PC window before More info is clicked: only a More info link and Don't run.
shots.notes: The SmartScreen dialog as it first appears, before More info is clicked (a More info link and only Don't run). Capture the dialog only (Win+Shift+S, window snip), no desktop around it.

shots.alt: The Nook installer wizard on its first page.
shots.notes: Run Nook-Windows-0.2.1-setup.exe past SmartScreen and capture the first page of the installer window (not the last). Window snip, 100 % scale.

shots.alt: The Nook icon in the Windows notification area with its context menu open.
shots.notes: Windows 11, dark taskbar, 100 % scale. Open the hidden-icons chevron, right-click the Nook icon so its menu is open, then snip the menu plus the icon row (Win+Shift+S rectangle). Needs the real tray.

shots.alt: File Explorer open at the Nook folder in LocalAppData, showing the log file and the bin folder.
shots.notes: File Explorer at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nook (type it in the address bar), details view so file names and sizes show. Hide your user name in the address bar if it is visible (blur or crop).

shots.alt: The Nook log file open in Notepad: one line per event, with the time first.
shots.notes: nook.log open in Notepad (dark theme), text area only: crop out the title bar, menu and toolbar row, which show the account picture.

shots.alt: Claude Code's /hooks screen listing Nook's relay on the hook events.
shots.notes: Install the hooks, start `claude` in a terminal, type /hooks and capture the list that shows the nook-hook.exe entries. Use a dark terminal at a readable font size; crop to the list. Hide any private path.

shots.alt: Cursor's hooks settings showing Nook's entries after the install.
shots.notes: After Settings -> Cursor -> Install hooks and a restart of Cursor, open Cursor's Hooks view (Cursor Settings) and capture the list with Nook's entries. Crop to the panel.

shots.alt: Windows Settings, Privacy and security, Camera, with 'Let desktop apps access your camera' turned on.
shots.notes: Windows 11 Settings -> Privacy & security -> Camera, scrolled so the 'Let desktop apps access your camera' switch is visible and on. Light or dark, 100 % scale.

shots.alt: The Nook agents list window next to a desktop, listing running sessions with their states.
shots.notes: In the real app turn on Settings -> Agents list with 3-4 real or fake-session sessions (npm run fake-session) so the small agents window shows rows. Snip the window with a bit of desktop around it; use the Nook wallpaper or a plain one. Not capturable in a plain browser.

shots.alt: Claude Code asking for permission in a terminal while the real Nook island shows the same request at the top of the screen.
shots.notes: Real Windows 11 desktop, a Claude Code permission prompt waiting in Windows Terminal and the real island open on the same request above it (use a throwaway project; no private paths, no other windows). Crop to the top of the screen and the terminal.

shots.alt: A Claude Code command prompt in Windows Terminal, with the same request in the island above it: Deny or Allow.
shots.notes: Real Windows 11 desktop, a Claude Code PowerShell command prompt waiting in Windows Terminal and the real island open on the same request above it (throwaway project, no private paths). Crop to the top of the screen and the prompt.

shots.alt: The island's session list with Claude Code and Cursor rows, the filter chips and the sparkle and cube marks.
shots.notes: Real Nook with one Claude Code session and one Cursor agent session running (Cursor hooks installed). Open the island on Home / the session list so both rows show; snip the island with 30 px around it over the Nook wallpaper or a plain desktop.
